change.author: Carina Wollendorfer

findings.title: Team admins are rejected: isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner only lets owners through
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` joins two checks with `&&` (lines 46-48). `isTeamAdmin` (packages/lib/server/queries/teams/index.ts:264-284) is true for role ADMIN or OWNER, and `isTeamOwner` (teams/index.ts:286-295) is true only for OWNER. So the conjunction is true only for owners, and a team ADMIN who is not the organizer or an attendee gets FORBIDDEN. The variable name and the intent point to `||`. Change `&&` to `||`. Also add a test for the ADMIN case (see the tests finding).

findings.title: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check is case-sensitive and skips base-email normalisation
findings.body: The blacklist is lowercased on the env side (line 71) but the candidate `guest` is compared as typed (line 77). `Spam@Example.com` passes a blacklist entry `spam@example.com`. The sibling path normalises both sides: handleNewBooking.ts:741-743 uses `extractBaseEmail(guest).toLowerCase()` and checkIfBookerEmailIsBlocked.ts:17-19 compares lowercased values. Normalise `guest` the same way (lowercase, and base email if the sibling applies it) before the `includes` check.

findings.title: Calendar update failure is swallowed after the attendee rows are already committed
findings.body: The handler writes the new attendees to the DB (lines 92-106) before updating the calendar. `updateCalendarAttendees` returns void (packages/core/EventManager.ts:596-602) and discards the per-calendar results. `updateAllCalendarEvents` catches its own errors and returns failure objects instead of throwing (EventManager.ts:921-938). So when a calendar update fails, the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` and the user sees success. The guests are never added to the calendar event. A retry does not fix it: the dedupe at lines 74-78 now drops those emails and the call fails with BAD_REQUEST (lines 80-81). The sibling editLocation.handler.ts:107-111 inspects `results` and logs on failure. Check the results here and surface the failure, or make the DB write and calendar sync reconcile on retry.

findings.title: Emails are sent to the raw input list, not to the guests actually added
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw `guests` input, not `uniqueGuests`. An email that already belongs to an attendee is dropped from `uniqueGuests` (lines 74-78) but is still in `guests`. In email-manager.ts:541-545 that attendee is then matched by `newGuests.includes` and gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail` ("Your event has been scheduled") instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Pass `uniqueGuests` (the emails actually inserted) so only new guests get the scheduled invite.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore the event type's disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: `sendLocationChangeEmails` (lines 495-524) gates the host and attendee emails on `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` (lines 503, 515; helpers at lines 81-87). `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no metadata and sends to the organizer, team members and every attendee unconditionally. The handler does not pass the event type metadata either (addGuests.handler.ts:168). The sibling editLocation.handler.ts:135-138 passes `booking?.eventType?.metadata`. An event type that disabled host or attendee emails will still receive 'Guests added' mail. Add an `eventTypeMetadata` parameter, gate the two branches the same way, and pass `booking.eventType?.metadata` from the handler.

findings.title: Question: should any booking attendee be able to add guests?
findings.body: The route is `authedProcedure` (_router.tsx:79), not `bookingsProcedure` like `editLocation` (_router.tsx:62). `bookingsProcedure` (util.ts:19-30) only lets the organizer or a collective-event member load the booking. This handler also accepts any user whose session email matches an attendee's email (line 52). Each call then does four things: it inserts attendee rows, updates calendar invites, sends mail to all attendees with `from: organizer.name` (attendee-scheduled-email.ts:50), and has no cap on the `guests` array (addGuests.schema.ts:5). Attendee emails are not necessarily verified, and the PR body does not say whether this is intended. Did you mean organizer and team admin/owner only? If attendees are meant to have this right, consider a cap on `guests` and a rate limit, since the handler sends one email per attendee.

findings.title: No booking status or time check, but the menu offers the action for past and unconfirmed bookings
findings.body: The handler loads the booking by id only (lines 26-42) and never checks status or end time. The Edit menu that holds 'Add guests' is shown for past confirmed bookings (BookingListItem.tsx:554) and for past pending, unconfirmed bookings (BookingListItem.tsx:553). For a past event, guests are invited and 'scheduled' mail goes out for a meeting that has already happened. For an unconfirmed booking there are usually no calendar references, so `updateCalendarAttendees` returns early (EventManager.ts:597-600) and only the emails go out. editLocation has the same exposure, so this is a gap in the sibling pattern as well as in this PR. Decide whether add-guests should be limited to upcoming accepted bookings.

findings.title: Server does not reject duplicate emails within one request
findings.body: The client rejects duplicates (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29), but the server schema accepts `z.array(z.string().email())` (addGuests.schema.ts:5) and the dedupe at lines 74-78 only compares against existing attendees. Duplicate inputs, from a direct tRPC call, both reach `createMany` (lines 100-104) and create duplicate attendee rows. Deduplicate `uniqueGuests` and probably make the schema reject duplicates.

findings.title: FORBIDDEN message uses a translation key that is not in common.json
findings.body: The handler throws `message: "you_do_not_have_permission"` (line 55). That key is not in apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json, and the dialog displays it through `t(err.message)` (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43). A user who hits this sees the raw key. Add the key to common.json or reuse an existing one.

findings.title: Validation error stays visible after a successful add and across reopen
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set to true when validation fails (line 56) and is reset only by Cancel (line 91). `onSuccess` (lines 36-41) closes the dialog and resets the emails but not `isInvalidEmail`. The component stays mounted in every BookingListItem (BookingListItem.tsx:357-361), so after a fix-and-submit the 'Emails must be unique and valid' message is still shown the next time the dialog opens. The close path via `onOpenChange` (line 61, Escape or overlay) also does not reset the emails or the error, unlike Cancel (lines 89-93). Reset `isInvalidEmail` in `onSuccess`, and reset the form in `onOpenChange` too.

findings.title: Unreachable fallback and schema rebuilt on every render
findings.body: `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is always a non-empty string, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback on line 44 can never run. The zod schema on line 26 is also built inside the component body and re-created on every render. Move it to module scope and drop the dead fallback, or use the fallback for a missing message.

findings.title: Hard-coded English 'Remove email' tooltip
findings.body: The remove-button tooltip on line 46 is a literal English string, while the rest of the dialog uses `t()`. Use a translation key and add it to common.json.

findings.title: No tests for the new handler or dialog
findings.body: The diff adds no test file for addGuests.handler.ts or AddGuestsDialog.tsx. The permission logic (see the `&&` finding) and the dedupe and blacklist logic are the parts most likely to regress, and a unit test for the ADMIN role would catch the first one.

contracts.action: Edit menu item 'Add guests' opens AddGuestsDialog
contracts.before_after: Same editBookingActions array and same pattern as 'change_location' (set state, open dialog). The new item is also shown under Edit for past confirmed bookings and for past unconfirmed bookings (BookingListItem.tsx:553-554), so it is not limited to upcoming accepted bookings.
contracts.visible_effect: A new 'Add guests' entry appears under Edit. Clicking it opens the dialog with one empty email field.

contracts.action: Submit in AddGuestsDialog calls trpc viewer.bookings.addGuests
contracts.before_after: editLocation uses bookingsProcedure (util.ts:19-65), which loads the booking only for the organizer or a collective member and returns UNAUTHORIZED otherwise. addGuests uses authedProcedure (_router.tsx:79) and does its own checks in the handler (addGuests.handler.ts:46-56). It admits attendees by email match, and its team check is wrong (the && finding). Neither path checks booking status.
contracts.visible_effect: Success: toast 'Guests added', dialog closes, bookings list invalidated (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36-41). Error: toast 'CODE: message' (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43-44).
contracts.failure_mode: Team ADMIN gets FORBIDDEN. The FORBIDDEN text is a raw key. If the calendar sync throws, the rows are already saved and the success path is not reached either way (see the handler contract).

contracts.action: addGuestsHandler writes attendees, updates the calendar, sends emails
contracts.before_after: editLocation checks updatedResult.results and logs on failure (lines 107-114), and passes event type metadata to the email step (135-138). addGuests does neither: it ignores the calendar result (165), and the email step gets no metadata (168). The DB write (92-106) happens before the calendar update, and editLocation writes its DB row after the calendar update.
contracts.visible_effect: Always 'Guests added' on success, even when the calendar invite was not updated.
contracts.failure_mode: Calendar failure is silent: updateCalendarAttendees does not throw (EventManager.ts:596-602) and updateAllCalendarEvents returns failures instead of throwing (EventManager.ts:921-938). A retry is rejected with BAD_REQUEST because the guests now exist (addGuests.handler.ts:74-81), so the calendar is never reconciled for the session.

contracts.action: sendAddGuestsEmails sends organizer, team and attendee emails
contracts.before_after: sendLocationChangeEmails checks eventTypeDisableHostEmail and eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail before sending (503, 515). sendAddGuestsEmails never checks them and takes no metadata. The attendee split on newGuests (541-545) sends AttendeeScheduledEmail to new guests and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail to existing attendees. Passing raw guests (168) misroutes resubmitted existing attendees.
contracts.visible_effect: Organizer and attendees receive 'Guests added' or 'scheduled' mail even when the event type disabled standard emails.
contracts.failure_mode: Errors are caught in the handler (addGuests.handler.ts:167-171) and logged with a generic message; the user still sees success.

contracts.action: Dialog local state (emails, isInvalidEmail) across submit, cancel and close
contracts.before_after: Cancel resets emails and error, then closes. onSuccess resets emails but not the error. onOpenChange (Escape or overlay) closes without any reset.
contracts.visible_effect: After a validation error is fixed and the add succeeds, the red error text is still shown the next time the dialog opens. Escape or overlay close keeps partially typed emails.

contracts.before_after: Same next/dynamic pattern with no loading placeholder. Until the chunk loads, the field area renders nothing.
contracts.visible_effect: The email input area is blank for a moment the first time the dialog opens.
contracts.failure_mode: If the chunk fails to load, nothing is rendered and there is no error message. This is the same as the existing PhoneInput and AddressInput wrappers.

contracts.action: Attendee and organizer add-guests email templates
contracts.before_after: Same wrapper pattern: a title key and a subject key are passed through {...props}. BaseScheduledEmail translates the title (BaseScheduledEmail.tsx:56-62). The subject key goes into BaseEmailHtml unchanged (BaseScheduledEmail.tsx:55), which is also true of the location-change sibling.
contracts.visible_effect: The body title is translated. The HTML document subject is the raw key, the same as the sibling.

summary: Reviewed the 15 files in this part (add-guests dialog, booking menu item, tRPC route and handler, email manager and templates, MultiEmail UI and locale keys). Main problems: the team-role check uses `&&` and so blocks team admins; the blacklist check is case-sensitive; calendar update failures are silent after the attendee rows are already saved, which blocks retry; emails go to the raw input list rather than the guests actually added; add-guests emails ignore the event type's disableStandardEmails settings; and the dialog keeps a stale validation error after a successful add. Also open for the author: whether any booking attendee should be allowed to add guests, since the sibling editLocation route is restricted to the organizer and collective members. Nothing was built or run; all findings come from reading the code.
